subject.title: Feature: Webchat / Control UI inline button support (buttons parameter, callback RPC, capabilities config)

question: Should WebChat inline interactions use the shared typed `presentation` action contract plus an authenticated `chat.callback` Gateway RPC, and should v1 add any WebChat capability/config key?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the first implementation would commit OpenClaw to a public WebChat/Gateway interaction contract and callback security model.

options.title: Adopt typed presentation RPC v1
options.body: Use final-only typed presentation/action blocks, add an authenticated `chat.callback` method, implement Control UI rendering, and keep webhook routing out of v1.

options.title: Split protocol before UI
options.body: Approve and land the Gateway protocol/callback authorization contract first, then add Control UI rendering in a follow-up.

options.title: Preserve legacy buttons compatibility
options.body: Support a legacy `buttons` shape alongside presentation, accepting a broader migration and long-term dual-contract surface.

recommendation.title: Adopt typed presentation RPC v1
recommendation.body: Use final-only typed presentation/action blocks, add an authenticated `chat.callback` method, implement Control UI rendering, and keep webhook routing out of v1.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal across the typed presentation contract and related Gateway/UI chat surfaces.
